articles.title: Stella McCartney makes waves with ‘sea life, not sea food’ theme in zero-wool Paris show
articles.summary: Designer showcases wool alternatives and ocean-inspired clothes and says ‘kindness requires real work’ Stella McCartney has been talking about animal rights at fashion week for 30 years. She is usually a lone voice, but the issue is back in the headlines this season.
body: “There is no wool on the runway this season, and I’m proud of that,” McCartney said after her show. She has been working on wool alternatives, including Brewed Protein, a fermented alternative to cashmere and wool developed in collaboration with the Japanese biotech firm Spiber, which was first used in her collections a year ago.

The issue, she says, is “a tricky one. I’ve got alpacas at home, and I have to shear them. If you can shear a sheep in a kind, humane way, then I don’t, personally, think that’s the end of the world. When we do have wool in our collections it is responsibly sourced. But the way a lot of [wool production] is done today is deeply cruel.

“At the end of the day it’s about how kind you are, but monitoring that kindness requires real work. At Stella, we police everything from start to finish at my cost, at my time. If I use wool, I can show you exactly where it’s coming from, and I’m proud of that. But I’m alone in that, and I shouldn’t be.”

articles.title: My mother’s phone calls became stranger, but I couldn’t visit. A rescue dog helped me reach her
articles.summary: Conversation was difficult. But Sally, a dear old German shepherd, gave me a glimpse of my mother’s emotional state. My mother had been wanting a dog for years. She lived in Perth, on the other side of the country to her children and grandchildren who were all grown up.
body: What I didn’t know was that the forbidding fence he was building, the gate operated by keypad and code, wasn’t just to contain a dog. It was to contain my mother.

Dogs became scarce during the Covid pandemic. There wasn’t much on offer at the local pound. In the winter of 2020, my mother and stepfather drove for several hours to collect Sally from a rescue shelter in a distant town. She was a chunky, ageing German shepherd, perhaps 10 or 11, with dense black fur and a grey muzzle, hard of hearing and stiff in the hips. Sally had been let go from a farm as she could no longer jump into the back of the ute. My stepfather lifted her on to a picnic blanket on the backseat of the car and they drove her home.
A few days later I rang my mother to ask about the new dog. “It’s a little yellow puppy,” she said. “It’s very naughty, but it might be better when its tapes have been tied.”

articles.title: BBC removes article linking bare nails trend to ‘white supremacist standards of beauty’
articles.summary: Corporation says story did not meet editorial standards after it attracts criticism from US and UK media. A BBC article that included a claim that a trend for bare nails was linked to “white supremacist standards of beauty” has been permanently removed from its website, after editors concluded it…
body: The article, which first ran on the BBC’s website on 27 September, examined an apparent “viral craze” for bare rather than decorated nails. It said the trend had been flooding social media and fashion catwalks.
It also covered criticisms of the trend, which suggested it could “stigmatise bold manicures”. The article noted that nail art had its roots in black, Latino and Asian communities.

In an early section of the article, it quoted the beauty journalist Kristina Rodulfo as saying: “That trend really promotes blankness and this kind of sameness and erasure of culture and identity that is so important to black and brown communities.
“They are often called elegant or tasteful and these are often usually euphemisms that perpetuate white supremacist standards of beauty.”

articles.title: Colman Domingo on the Elegance of All-Black Luggage
articles.summary: The star of Euphoria, Sing Sing, and The Four Seasons' travel hacks include J.Crew-taught folding skills, packing cubes full of fragrances, and plenty of gummy bears.
body: Colman Domingo is always on the move. The Emmy-winning actor kicked off our call by warning me that the famed bells of Reykjavik may ring in the background during our chat—having arrived in Iceland after a quick turnaround from Santa Fe, jet-setting from one location to another to film the third season of his Netflix hit The Four Seasons, along with co-stars Tina Fey, Will Forte, Kerri Kenney-Silver, Marco Calvani, and Erika Henningsen.

“I move pretty quickly,” the 56-year-old Philadelphia native told Condé Nast Traveler. As a result, there's one aspect of travel he's totally mastered: “I'm very proud of my packing style—I’ve got it down to a science.”

Case in point: He only had a few hours at home between those trips, having arrived back in Malibu from New Mexico at 10:30 p.m. before a morning flight to Iceland. But that was plenty of time for the pro. “We got in, did laundry, packed, and were in bed by 11:45 p.m.,” he said.

It all stems from the precision he learned during his early jobs at J. Crew and Banana Republic. “Everything is very organized and well-folded—I love packing like I’m still working there,” he said. “I’m pretty detailed about my packing.”
points: The star of Euphoria, Sing Sing, and The Four Seasons' travel hacks include J.Crew-taught folding skills, packing cubes full of fragrances, and plenty of gummy bears.

articles.title: 20 Years After Eat, Pray, Love, Bali Is Still Worth a Wellness Trip
articles.summary: As Elizabeth Gilbert’s groundbreaking memoir turns two decades old, a writer who’s tried them all shares her favorite Bali resorts for a soulful wellness reset.
body: Even before Elizabeth Gilbert wrote about studying with a Balinese medicine man and a female Balinese traditional healer in her bestselling 2006 memoir Eat, Pray, Love, the Indonesian island was already earning a reputation as a wellness destination. Back then, yoga and meditation, powerful and intuitive massage, herbal treatments inspired by centuries-old rituals of Balinese royalty and, of course, the mysterious local energy healers known as balian drew intrepid pre–smartphone era travelers.

Twenty years after the book, however, Bali is no longer a wellness destination but the definitive global destination for wellbeing—in virtually every form, woo-woo to cutting edge. The evolution was slow, until it wasn’t: In 2014, fresh off a breakup and recently laid off—embarrassingly cliché, right?—I chose Bali for my first-ever solo trip and within days was practicing chaturanga dandasana at The Yoga Barn, whispering wishes before intricately carved water spouts at Tirta Empul water temple, and getting deliciously deep massages ( pijat ) from sweet Balinese women for about $6.
points: As Elizabeth Gilbert’s groundbreaking memoir turns two decades old, a writer who’s tried them all shares her favorite Bali resorts for a soulful wellness reset.

articles.title: This Cookbook Author Bride Held a Five-Hour Dinner Party for Her Intimate Provence Wedding
articles.summary: Chloé Crane-Leroux and Clément Leclerc embraced the spirit and cuisine of Provence at their 30-person wedding within the grounds of an 18th-century villa.
body: Then the pandemic hit and Chloé returned to Canada—where the childhood friends matched on a dating app. “We both messaged each other some version of ‘long time no see,’ met up in a park, and have been tied at the hip ever since,” says Clément. He followed Chloé back to New York and the two quickly began laying down roots in the city. “It was clear to us that even though this became real in 2020, our relationship had been in the works for decades,” he says.

When choosing where to tie the knot, Provence was really the only place the couple had in mind. “Provence has become such an important part of our story,” explains Chloé. “Over time, we’ve also developed a beautiful relationship with the family behind the Domaines de Chabran. We stay with them whenever we’re in Provence, so when it came time to choose where we would get married, it almost felt inevitable. Mas de Chabran already felt like home.” The pair took over the location on September 12, 2026 to host an intimate 30-person celebration with additional events throughout the weekend.

articles.title: 6 Best AHA Body Lotions for Smoother Skin All Over
articles.summary: The best AHA body lotions use glycolic and lactic acids to resurface skin and address issues like keratosis pilaris and rough skin. Shop our top picks.
body: Exfoliation for the body isn’t exactly new (see: body scrubs ), but alpha hydroxy acids (AHAs) take the concept to the next level. AHA body lotions pair these chemical exfoliants with rich, buttery bases to gently resurface skin and replenish moisture in a single step, streamlining your routine while smoothing and softening skin.

If you’re content with your current body lotion, that’s great. In fact, “not everyone needs an AHA body lotion,” says Tiffany Libby, MD, a board-certified dermatologist in Providence. However, she says they can be especially helpful if you have rough or bumpy texture like keratosis pilaris, hyperpigmentation or dullness, crepiness, or fine lines. “AHAs work by loosening the bonds between dead skin cells, helping them shed more efficiently, so the skin feels smoother and looks more even,” says Dr. Libby.
points: The best AHA body lotions use glycolic and lactic acids to resurface skin and address issues like keratosis pilaris and rough skin.

articles.title: How to Sign up for Amazon's ‘Invite-Only’ Deals During October Prime Day
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Not all Prime Day deals are open to just anybody. Since 2023, some of the best offers in Amazon's biggest sales are invite-only—meaning you have to sign up for them in advance of the sale going live, and hope you get chosen to receive the discount.
body: Find an "Invite-Only Prime Deal" that you want to purchase. You can find these deals listed on the Deals page once Prime Day begins.

You will receive an email notification confirming that you requested an invite. The confirmation will be sent to the email that is on your Amazon account. If you don't have an email on your account, add one by navigating to Your Account > Login > Security.

Keep in mind that just because you requested an invitation doesn't mean you'll receive one. If you are selected, you'll receive both a push notification in the Amazon app and email notifying you during the sale. If you're not selected, Amazon will also let you know you didn't get one. You can only buy one of the products that you were invited for, but you can request as many different product invitations as you want. The invitation will last as long as the sale lasts, or as long as there is stick remaining.

articles.title: A Close Look At the 7 Key Autumn/Winter 2026 Bag Trends
articles.summary: Vogue highlights the key fall 2026 handbag trends to shop now. From super shoulder bags to new-gen clutches, these are styles to bookmark now.
body: Compared with the wave of house debuts for spring/summer, the fall/winter 2026 season was business as usual—sort of. Only a handful of inaugural showcases this time around, but the sophomore collections brought plenty of ideas to the fore, including an abundance of ready-to-wear and bag trends.

Pieter Mulier focused on the former in his last show for Alaïa after a five-year stint, which Vogue ’s Sarah Mower described as “quiet perfectionism”. “It’s just really clothes for real people, not for an image,” Mulier said. “To reduce, reduce. No bags, no jewelry. Only beauty and clothes and a naked shoe. Because that’s what Azzedine was.”

Yet, during his tenure, Mulier delivered a number of It-bags, the most recent being his Le Teckel—meaning “sausage dog” in French, for its slimline shape—which will hold its value far beyond his departure. In fact, he could be credited with influencing the current streamlined, top-handle bag trend —the east-west —designed with the same tuck-under-your-arm spirit as the Le Teckel—which was present across recent runway shows.
